Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marcus Chen (Redwood CSM), Maya Rivera (Auriga Channel Lead), Tom Okoye (Auriga VP Partnerships), Lena Ortiz (Auriga SE), Ravi Mehta (Auriga Sales Ops)
summary: Weekly co-sell / pipeline review focusing on three joint opportunities: NovaHealth (pilot scoping), Meridian Retail (evaluation), and Zenith SaaS (RFP). Discussed next steps for GTM materials, technical benchmarking, and exec introductions. Agreed to run a short Dedicated vs Hosted benchmark and to sync on pricing approach for pilot deals.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, we'll kick off. Quick roll call?
[00:05] Maya Rivera: Hi, Maya here.
[00:07] Tom Okoye: Tom on the line.
[00:09] Lena Ortiz: Lena.
[00:11] Ravi Mehta: Ravi — good afternoon.
[00:13] Priya Nair: Priya from Redwood. Marcus here for support.
[00:16] Marcus Chen: Hey all.
[00:20] Jordan Lee: Awesome. Agenda, three main deals — NovaHealth pilot, Meridian Retail evaluation, Zenith RFP. Quick health updates then action items. Maya, want to start with NovaHealth?
[00:28] Maya Rivera: Yeah, NovaHealth is moving fast, they want a two-week pilot, security is a gating factor — they asked about SOC 2, SAML SSO, and KMS. We shared the security pack but they want sample audit logs and an on-prem option is on the table.
[00:44] Priya Nair: Right, we have Private deployment and VPC options, and audit logs are part of our offering. Small caveat, the on-prem package timeline is a bit longer but for pilot we can propose a Private VPC in their preferred cloud. There's some nuance around HSM integration for their KMS requirement.
[01:03] Tom Okoye: For pricing, NovaHealth is sensitive to per-token cost; they asked if we can do a pilot discount and a path to Dedicated later.
[01:11] Jordan Lee: We can do a pilot credit + committed Dedicated pricing conversation post-pilot. Important to set success criteria — latency under 300ms p95 on clinical note generation and cost per 1k tokens under X.
[01:23] Lena Ortiz: On the SAML/SSO note, they use Okta; we've done Okta SAML with other health customers but some of the SCIM provisioning gaps came up earlier — we should flag that.
[01:35] Priya Nair: Agree. I'll prepare a short checklist for NovaHealth: SOC 2 + audit sample, SSO/SCIM notes, KMS/HSM support, and a sample latency/cost target.
[01:46] Jordan Lee: Great. Meridian Retail?
[01:48] Maya Rivera: They moved to a POC but asked about embeddings indexing and vector store compatibility — they use Pinecone today and we pitched Redwood embeddings plus caching. Concerned about re-indexing cost and search latency.
[02:00] Priya Nair: We can demonstrate our caching and prefix KV approaches to avoid re-indexing for incremental updates; latency-wise our hosted embeddings + Redis cache has been within their SLA for other retail workloads. Need sample corpus to validate.
[02:15] Ravi Mehta: Meridian asked about data residency — EMEA accounts require EU-only data processing.
[02:20] Jordan Lee: We have EU regions but for Dedicated/Private we can guarantee EU-only routing. We'll need an SO for data residency in the contract, Marcus can add that to the template.
[02:29] Marcus Chen: I'll add a clause template for EU data residency and circulate.
[02:33] Maya Rivera: Zenith SaaS — RFP went out; they have heavy security and legal asks plus an evaluation window in three weeks. They listed competitors Anthropic and Vertex; they want to see performance benchmarks and a pricing model.
[02:45] Jordan Lee: For RFP, we'll need a short one-page performance summary plus bench numbers. Priya, can you spin up a 1-hour test against Zenith's sample prompts? We should include both Hosted and Dedicated numbers and a fallback plan if latency spikes.
[03:00] Priya Nair: Yes, but we need the sample prompts and expected concurrency. If they want p95 under 250ms at 50 RPS that's a different bar.
[03:09] Lena Ortiz: I can get sample prompts. Also, small note — the RFP questioned our model catalog, they asked which model variants we verify. They called out hallucination risk on long-context summarization.
[03:21] Jordan Lee: Good point. We'll include model recommendations and quantization/latency tradeoffs. For hallucination, include our eval harness and a plan for prompt guardrails and reranking.
[03:31] Tom Okoye: On co-sell motion, internally we need to align on references and revenue split. Auriga will introduce Redwood to their top 10 targets; we need a simple rev share framework.
[03:42] Jordan Lee: We have a partner rev-share template; I'll share and we can customize. Also, for top accounts we'll propose an SPR (sales playbook) and joint exec email. Marcus will own the cadence.
[03:54] Marcus Chen: I'll set up a 30-day co-sell cadence in the partnership CRM and propose exec intro emails.
[04:02] Maya Rivera: Two quick asks from our side — 1) a short technical runbook for Aurora sales engineers that explains Redwood's Dedicated vs Hosted decision tree, and 2) an enablement recording for sales reps.
[04:13] Priya Nair: We have an enablement deck; I'll produce a condensed runbook — decision tree, security checkpoints, and typical pricing bands for pilot vs committed Dedicated.
[04:23] Jordan Lee: Great. Any risks we haven't covered?
[04:27] Lena Ortiz: Potential risk — capacity fragmentation if multiple Auriga accounts want Dedicated but low commit. Need a clear policy on bursts and shared pools.
[04:36] Priya Nair: We'll propose a burst policy and minimum baseline for Dedicated. For lower commit we can do hosted with burst guarantees.
[04:44] Tom Okoye: One more — the procurement timeline for Zenith is compressed; they asked for contract redlines within five business days.
[04:51] Jordan Lee: Our legal has a fast-track partner review path but we'll need early redline visibility. Marcus, can you coordinate with legal?
[04:57] Marcus Chen: Yep, will loop in legal and Auriga ops.
[05:00] Jordan Lee: Ok, quick recap and next steps: Jordan to share GTM deck; Priya to run benchmarks; Marcus to add contract templates and cadence; Maya to intro accounts. We'll aim to reconvene in one week unless there are blockers.
[05:13] Maya Rivera: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[05:15] Jordan Lee: Thanks, bye.
[05:16] [meeting ended]
